newsitem.title: USA: Dow sells off after Boeing opens.
newsitem.headline: Dow sells off after Boeing opens.

text.p: The Dow industrials lost ground rapidly in morning trading when Boeing Co opened lower after reporting weaker than forecast first quarter operating earnings.
The bond market offered little help and stayed lower after March new home sales came in at a bigger than forecast 813,000 while the February number was revised upward to 834,000 from 811,000.
The Dow was down 36 points at 6703 while declines led advances by about nine to eight. Boeing was down seven at 95.
Boeing shaved 23 points off the Dow, analysts said.
The company reported first quarter operating profits of $0.87 a share compared with $0.35 a year ago. The First Call estimate was $1.00.
Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons, said that trading today would have been cautious even without the sell-off in Boeing.

"We have had three down days in a row, and tomorrow we have the (first quarter) employment cost index," he said. "We will have a modest downside until we see that figure. It could magnify fears of a rate increase."
U.S. Treasuries were unchanged to lower, with the long bond down 4/32 to yield 7.15 percent.
Weakness in the bond market also contributed to the soft tone of the stock market, said Jeffery M. Applegate, chief investment strategist at Lehman Brothers.
"We came back to fair value last week because of earnings. But compared to interest rates, stocks are still above fair value," Applegate said.
"If on any given day bonds don't act well, it will carry over into the stock market. That seems to be the case today. This makes it difficult for the equity market to go up."
